terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build Ambrose's rules here, run them, and change the slip's values to try each way through.

tasks.title: Say whether the clock is overdue
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/rules.cpp`, make a `bool` called `isOverdue`: `true` when the clock has been in the shop more days than promised (`daysInShop` and `promisedDays`), `false` otherwise. Then print exactly one of these two lines, chosen by `isOverdue`:

```
Status: overdue
Status: on time
```

Check runs your program with other days, the day it was promised among them, reads `isOverdue` and compares the lines your task printed.
nextSteps: Make `isOverdue` from a comparison of the two numbers.
Write an `if` on `isOverdue` with the overdue line in its `{ }`.
Add an `else` with the other line.
Change `daysInShop` to 7 for a moment, build, run, and read which line comes out.
hints: A comparison like `a > b` is a `bool` by itself: it is `true` or `false`, so it can be the value of `isOverdue`.
On the promised day the clock is on time. Only more days than promised make it overdue, so the comparison is "greater than", not "greater than or equal".
The shape is `bool isOverdue = daysInShop > promisedDays;`, then `if (isOverdue) { ... } else { ... }`.

tasks.title: Work out what the customer pays
tasks.description:
A repair is free when the clock was repaired here 12 months ago or less (`monthsSinceRepair`) and the same fault came back (`sameFault`). Under `// Task 2`, make a `double` called `toPay`: `0` when the repair is free, `quote` otherwise. Print it:

```
To pay: 45.5
```

Check runs your program with other slips, at exactly 12 months among them, reads `toPay` and compares the line.
nextSteps: Make `toPay` before any `if`, with a first value.
Write the condition for a free repair: two things that must both be true.
Give `toPay` its other value inside the `if`.
Print `To pay: ` and `toPay` after the `if`, then build and run.
hints: A variable made inside `{ }` is gone after the `}`. `toPay` has to be printed after the `if`, so make it before.
`&&` joins two conditions into one that is true only when both are. 12 months ago still counts, so compare with `<=`.
The shape is `double toPay = quote;`, then `if (monthsSinceRepair <= 12 && sameFault) { toPay = 0; }`.

tasks.title: Pick the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `bool` called `isRush`: `true` when the customer needs the clock back in 2 days or fewer (`daysUntilNeeded`), or when it is for an event (`forEvent`). Then print exactly one of these two lines, chosen by `isRush`:

```
Shelf: rush
Shelf: normal
```

Check runs your program with other slips, needed in exactly 2 days among them, reads `isRush` and compares the line.
nextSteps: Write the two reasons for the rush shelf as two conditions.
Join them so that either one is enough, and make `isRush` from that.
Try `forEvent = true` with many days, build and run.
hints: Either reason is enough on its own. That is a different joining word than in Task 2.
`||` is true when at least one side is true. "2 days or fewer" includes 2.
The shape is `bool isRush = daysUntilNeeded <= 2 || forEvent;`, then an `if` and an `else`.

tasks.title: Say where the bench is
tasks.description:
The benches are numbered 1 to 6, and 0 means Kasimir has not given one yet. Under `// Task 4`, print exactly one line, chosen by `bench`:

```
Bench: not given yet        when bench is 0
Bench: 3                    when bench is 1 to 6, with its own number
Bench: no such bench        for any other number
```

Check runs your program with other benches, 0, 1 and 6 among them, and compares the line.
nextSteps: Start with the case of bench 0: compare `bench` with 0.
Add an `else if` for a real bench, 1 to 6.
Finish with an `else` for every other number.
Build and read every warning before you run: one of them may be about this task.
hints: Comparing for equal takes two equals signs. A single one gives `bench` a new value, and the compiler warns about it.
`if`, `else if` and `else` are tried from the top, and only the first one that is true runs. "1 to 6" is two comparisons joined with `&&`.
The shape is `if (bench == 0) { ... } else if (bench >= 1 && bench <= 6) { ... } else { ... }`.
